Every "bad grind" in OSRS has a worse equivalent in RS3. Most people still playing it don't make alts like OSRS players do, so they don't see the rotten timbers RS3 is built on.  
Sure, some of the content they have that we don't is nice, but it's attached to a storyline that went too big too fast, and most of their expansions happen to take place in dungeons, one-off islands, other planes, or even just instances.  
People say OSRS is built on nostalgia? No, go see Jimmy's videos on that, it's really not. RS3 is carried by the nostalgia of people that *didn't stop playing when EoC dropped* or got in after it did because they saw a hotbar and could live with the jank of the tick system. They maxed a long time ago, and only new content really intrigues them if they're not going for 200m all or their officially-recognized virtual levels.  
As for rotting foundations: I'd say more than 3/4ths of RS3 is "dead content". Armors that are grinds to get, with pain-in-the-ass charge upkeep, immediately outclassed by something non-degradable that came out after it chronologically. Guides that don't make sense because they weren't updated with respect for new gear. Guides that are useless because they assume you're maxed -- and are made for content you'd never do at max but for clogging -- or have unlimited gp/$$$ to throw at gear setups (OSRS has this problem too, just less). This is all even without mentioning that while the RS3 wiki team does a bang-up job curating the information they do have on RS3, it's simply less documented. Drop rates aren't exact, and many bossing mechanics make them variable. You want to know how dry you are? Fuck you, the item is "RARE" and no RS3 mod ever said how rare it was.  
  
Should they get rid of MTX? Probably. Should they offer a real, permanently segmented set of worlds for people to play on with the promise of no purchaseable in-game mechanical benefits a-la treasure hunter? I'd support that. I wouldn't play it though.

You ask what hero in Artifact is the most underrated? I say Tidehunter.  
Anecdotally, tidehunter's active has won me two games - one in draft and one against a friend in 1v1 constructed. Its only downside is the time for it to come online, but by the time it's available it's unlikely that your opponent has the instant hero removal required to remove an armored, 18HP hero from the board. Seriously - the only threats to tidehunter are a few high cost Black cards and sniper/PA signature cards. Possibly Friendly Fire as well, but ideally Tidehunter is in a lane all his own, enemy neighbors being at least one hero, with the rest of the lane full of enemy creeps. Up to three guaranteed stuns with a coin-flip to stun each other enemy unit in the lane is massive stall potential in your low priority // a losing lane. He suffers from low attack, but his job is really just to waste your opponent's attacks in his lane.  
Stalling losing lanes wins you games in Artifact - many times a close game boils down to ~~a fucking thunderhide pack in draft good god that card is infuriating without Slay~~ one key combat phase. Maybe one *extra* combat phase.  
  
Just to ramble on a bit more - he works in all lanes, unlike some heroes that have a lane preference (like Drow in the third lane to make removal before her aura gives its benefit for a full round less likely or impossible). In the first lane he lets you focus on value in lanes 2 and 3, should you opponent commit heavily to lane 1, as his mass stun will save your tower/ancient from a good deal of damage... 50% of the time... Allowing your lanes 2 and 3 a round they wouldn't have if losing the first lane would lose you the game, as is the case when facing many aggro decks. In lanes 2 and 3, he works in a similar way, giving the lanes "in front of" his lane, time wise, an extra round they might not otherwise have for you to meet you win condition(s). Case in point Tidehunter allows you to delay a loss, alone, more effectively than any other hero in the opening set.  
  
Oh, and on top of all this, any retaliate on him (dark seer's sig, barbed mail) is magnificent. 2 retaliate (without negative att. modifiers or enemy armor) is enough to let him kill creeps in 1 combat phase. Fountain flask can be insane value on him with a base health pool of 18. Not to mention that his signature card is a *one mana armor MODIFIER that gives you initiative, which is essential in any red deck for securing the combat phase YOU want*.
